questions.stem: Name the enzyme that digests starch, and state the type of food molecule it produces.
markscheme: B1: amylase (accept carbohydrase)
B1: sugars (e.g. glucose or maltose)
questions.modelAnswer: Starch is digested by the enzyme amylase (a carbohydrase), which breaks the large starch molecule down into smaller sugar molecules such as maltose and glucose. This happens in the mouth and the small intestine.

questions.stem: State the function of red blood cells, and give one adaptation that helps them carry out this function.
markscheme: B1: carry oxygen around the body
B1: an adaptation, e.g. contains haemoglobin / no nucleus / biconcave shape / flexible membrane
questions.modelAnswer: Red blood cells carry oxygen from the lungs to respiring cells around the body. Adaptations include: a biconcave disc shape giving a large surface area for oxygen to diffuse across; haemoglobin, which binds the oxygen; no nucleus, leaving more space for haemoglobin; and a flexible membrane to squeeze through narrow capillaries. Any one of these earns the mark.

questions.stem: Name the vessels that carry water and dissolved mineral ions from the roots to the leaves, and name the process by which water vapour leaves the leaves.
markscheme: B1: xylem vessels
B1: transpiration
questions.modelAnswer: Water and dissolved mineral ions are carried up the plant from the roots to the leaves in the xylem vessels. Water then evaporates from the leaves and diffuses out as water vapour — this loss of water from the leaves is called transpiration.

questions.stem: A student finds a small animal with moist skin and no scales. It lays its eggs in water, and the young hatch into larvae that live in water. State the vertebrate group it belongs to, and give one other feature of this group.
markscheme: B1: amphibians (e.g. frog, toad or newt)
B1: another feature, e.g. metamorphosis from larva to adult / can breathe through the skin / cold-blooded
questions.modelAnswer: The animal is an amphibian (such as a frog, toad or newt): moist scale-less skin, jelly-like eggs laid in water, and aquatic larvae are all amphibian features. Another feature of the group is that the young undergo metamorphosis (a tadpole develops into an adult frog); amphibians are also cold-blooded and can exchange gases through their moist skin.

questions.stem: A student tests a food sample for reducing sugars. Describe the test, including the reagent used and the result of a positive test.
markscheme: B1: add Benedict's solution (reagent) to the sample
B1: heat the mixture in a water bath (about $75^{\circ}$C)
B1: a positive result changes from blue to orange/red (brick red)
questions.modelAnswer: Add Benedict's solution to the food sample (a few drops, and mix). Then heat the test tube gently in a water bath at about $75^{\circ}$C for a few minutes. If reducing sugars are present, the solution changes colour from blue to green, yellow, orange or brick red, depending on how much sugar is present. No sugar means it stays blue.

questions.stem: Blood leaving the right ventricle of the heart is pumped towards the lungs. (a) Name the vessel that carries this blood. (b) Explain what happens to the blood while it passes through the lungs.
markscheme: B1: the pulmonary artery
B1: oxygen is absorbed into the blood (from the air sacs)
B1: carbon dioxide is removed from the blood (into the air to be breathed out)
questions.modelAnswer: (a) The pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood from the right ventricle to the lungs. (b) In the lungs the blood passes close to the air sacs (alveoli): oxygen diffuses into the blood and binds to haemoglobin, while carbon dioxide diffuses out of the blood into the air to be breathed out. The blood returns to the heart via the pulmonary vein as oxygenated blood.

questions.stem: Decomposers break down dead organisms faster in warm, moist conditions than in cold, dry ones. Explain why, referring to the enzymes of the decomposers.
markscheme: B1: decomposers (bacteria and fungi) release enzymes to digest dead matter externally
B1: warmer temperatures increase the rate of enzyme activity / respiration, so digestion is faster
B1: moisture is needed for the enzymes / digestion to take place, so dry conditions slow decomposition
questions.modelAnswer: Decomposers such as bacteria and fungi release enzymes that digest the dead matter outside their cells, and they need water for this digestion to happen. Enzymes work faster at warmer temperatures (up to their optimum), because the molecules collide and react more often, and the decomposers' respiration and growth also speed up. In cold, dry conditions the enzymes work slowly and lack the water they need, so decomposition is much slower.

questions.stem: Explain how a developing baby (fetus) obtains oxygen from its mother. Refer to the placenta and the umbilical cord in your answer.
markscheme: B1: oxygen diffuses from the mother's blood into the baby's blood across the placenta
B1: the umbilical cord carries the oxygenated blood to the baby
B1: the mother's and baby's blood do not mix (they are kept separate in the placenta)
questions.modelAnswer: The fetus is joined to the mother by the umbilical cord, which connects to the placenta. In the placenta, the mother's blood and the baby's blood flow close together but never mix: oxygen (and dissolved nutrients) diffuse across the placenta from the mother's blood into the baby's blood, while carbon dioxide diffuses the other way to be removed by the mother. The oxygenated blood then travels to the baby through the umbilical cord.
